it gives us day and night, which helps plants and animals have a rhythm of activity and rest
it creates day and night, allowing time for work and rest
hints: Think about when plants grow and when animals sleep.
Day and night affect our activities.
questions.explanation: The earth's rotation causes day and night. This gives living things a regular pattern of light and darkness for activities and rest.
questions.misconception: The earth's rotation has no effect on life.

indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B5.3.1.1 Recognise that different parts of the human body work interdependently to perform a specific function
indicator.objective: Know the parts of the respiratory system in humans

questions.stem: Which organ is the main part of the respiratory system where air goes in?
questions.explanation: The nose is the main opening where air enters the respiratory system.
questions.misconception: The nose is not part of the respiratory system.

questions.stem: Which tube carries air from the nose to the lungs?
hints: It is also called the trachea.
questions.explanation: The windpipe (trachea) carries air from the nose to the lungs.

questions.stem: Which organs take oxygen from the air into the body?
hints: They expand when you breathe in.
questions.explanation: The lungs take oxygen from the air into the body.

questions.stem: Which muscle helps the lungs expand and contract during breathing?
hints: It moves up and down when you breathe.
questions.explanation: The diaphragm is the muscle below the lungs that helps them expand and contract.

questions.stem: What do the lungs do?
options: Take oxygen into the body and remove carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: The lungs take oxygen into the body and remove carbon dioxide.

questions.stem: What is one function of the nose in breathing?
options: It filters dust from the air
hints: Hairs in the nose trap dirt.
It cleans the air before it goes to the lungs.
questions.explanation: The nose filters dust from the air before it enters the lungs.
questions.misconception: The nose only helps you smell.

questions.stem: What is the function of the windpipe?
options: It carries air to the lungs
It carries food to the stomach
hints: It connects the nose to the lungs.
questions.explanation: The windpipe carries air from the nose to the lungs.

questions.stem: What does the diaphragm do during breathing?
options: It helps the lungs expand and contract
hints: It moves to help you breathe in and out.
questions.explanation: The diaphragm helps the lungs expand and contract during breathing.
questions.misconception: The diaphragm is not involved in breathing.

questions.stem: What happens when you breathe in?
questions.explanation: When you breathe in, air enters the lungs.
questions.misconception: Breathing in means air leaves the lungs.

questions.stem: Why are the lungs important?
options: They help the body get oxygen and remove carbon dioxide
hints: Carbon dioxide is a waste gas.
questions.explanation: The lungs are important because they help the body get oxygen and remove carbon dioxide.

questions.stem: Name two parts of the respiratory system.
questions.explanation: The main parts of the respiratory system include the nose, windpipe, lungs and diaphragm.
questions.misconception: Only the lungs are part of the respiratory system.

questions.stem: What happens when you breathe out?
answer: air is pushed out of the lungs
questions.explanation: When you breathe out, air (including carbon dioxide) leaves the lungs.
questions.misconception: Breathing out means air enters the lungs.

questions.stem: Explain why we should breathe through the nose rather than the mouth.
answer: the nose filters dust and warms the air before it reaches the lungs
the nose traps dust and dirt so the air is cleaner
breathing through the nose cleans and warms the air
hints: What do the hairs in the nose do?
questions.explanation: Breathing through the nose is better because the nose filters dust and warms the air before it reaches the lungs.
questions.misconception: The nose does not filter air.

questions.stem: What is the function of the windpipe?
answer: it carries air from the nose to the lungs
it is a tube that carries air to the lungs
it transports air to the lungs
hints: It connects the nose and lungs.
questions.explanation: The windpipe carries air from the nose to the lungs.

questions.stem: What is the function of the diaphragm?
answer: it helps the lungs expand and contract during breathing
it is a muscle that helps you breathe
it moves the lungs to help breathing
hints: It is a muscle below the lungs.
It helps you breathe in and out.
questions.explanation: The diaphragm is a muscle that helps the lungs expand and contract during breathing.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the function of the lungs?
options: They take in oxygen and remove carbon dioxide
They take in carbon dioxide and remove oxygen
They pump blood around the body
hints: Oxygen is needed by the body.
Carbon dioxide is a waste gas.
questions.explanation: The lungs take in oxygen and remove carbon dioxide from the body.
questions.misconception: The lungs take in carbon dioxide.

questions.stem: What happens to the diaphragm when you breathe in?
options: It moves down to help the lungs expand
It moves up to squeeze the lungs
hints: The lungs need to fill with air.
The diaphragm moves to make space.
questions.explanation: When you breathe in, the diaphragm moves down to help the lungs expand and fill with air.
questions.misconception: The diaphragm moves up when breathing in.

questions.stem: Draw a simple diagram of the respiratory system. Label the nose, windpipe, lungs and diaphragm.

criteria.description: Drew a simple diagram showing the respiratory system

hints: Start with the nose at the top.
The windpipe goes down to the lungs.
The diaphragm is below the lungs.
questions.explanation: This is a drawing task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.
questions.misconception: The lungs are in the stomach.

questions.stem: In groups, make a simple model of breathing using a plastic bottle, balloons and rubber bands. Show how the balloon (lung) inflates when you pull the rubber sheet (diaphragm) down. Describe what happens.

criteria.description: Built a simple model of the respiratory system
Showed the balloon inflating when the sheet was pulled down
Explained that the diaphragm moving down helps the lungs fill with air

hints: The bottle is like the chest.
The balloon is like the lung.
The rubber sheet is like the diaphragm.
questions.explanation: This is a practical task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.

questions.stem: Explain why the lungs are important for life.
answer: they take oxygen from the air into the body and remove carbon dioxide, which is needed for life
they help us breathe by taking in oxygen and removing carbon dioxide
the lungs supply oxygen to the body and remove waste carbon dioxide
hints: Carbon dioxide is a waste gas.
questions.explanation: The lungs are important because they supply oxygen to the body and remove carbon dioxide, which is necessary for life.
questions.misconception: The lungs are not important for life.

indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B5.3.2.1 Show understanding of the orderliness of the sun, planets and satellites in the solar system, as well as the important role of the sun in the existence of the solar system
indicator.objective: Identify the components of the solar system (sun, earth, moon, other planets, satellite)

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a component of the solar system?
hints: Which one is made by humans and does not orbit the sun?
A car stays on the ground.
questions.explanation: A car is not a component of the solar system. The sun, earth and moon are all parts of the solar system.
questions.misconception: Anything in the sky is part of the solar system.

questions.stem: Which of these is a planet?
hints: Mars is one of the planets.
questions.explanation: Mars is a planet. The sun is a star, and the moon is a satellite of the earth.

questions.stem: Name two components of the solar system.
hints: Think of the biggest object and the one we live on.
Think of what moves around the earth.
questions.explanation: The solar system includes the sun, planets (like earth), and satellites (like the moon).
questions.misconception: Only the sun is in the solar system.

questions.stem: Draw a simple diagram of the solar system. Show the sun at the centre, the earth, the moon, and at least two other planets. Label the sun, earth, moon and one other planet.

criteria.description: Drew the sun at the centre
Drew the earth and the moon
Drew at least two other planets
Labeled the sun, earth, moon and one other planet

hints: Put the sun in the middle.
The earth moves around the sun.
The moon moves around the earth.
questions.explanation: This is a drawing task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.
questions.misconception: The earth is at the centre of the solar system.

questions.stem: What is at the centre of the solar system?
hints: It is the biggest and brightest object.
questions.explanation: The sun is at the centre of the solar system. All planets move around the sun.
questions.misconception: The earth is at the centre of the solar system.

questions.stem: Which is the largest body in the solar system?
hints: It gives light and heat to all the planets.
questions.explanation: The sun is the largest body in the solar system.
questions.misconception: The earth is the largest body.

questions.stem: Why is the sun important in the solar system?
answer: it provides light and heat to the planets
it gives light and warmth to the solar system
it is the source of energy for the solar system
hints: What does the sun give to the planets?
questions.explanation: The sun is important because it provides light and heat energy to the planets in the solar system.

questions.stem: What do planets do in the solar system?
hints: The sun is at the centre.
Planets travel in paths around the sun.
questions.explanation: Planets move around the sun in the solar system.

questions.stem: Which of these is a planet that moves around the sun?
hints: It is one of the planets.
questions.explanation: Earth is a planet that moves around the sun.

questions.stem: Explain how planets move in the solar system.
answer: planets move in paths around the sun
planets travel around the sun in circular paths
hints: The sun is at the centre.
Planets do not move in straight lines away from the sun.
questions.explanation: Planets move in curved paths (orbits) around the sun, which is at the centre of the solar system.

questions.stem: Is the earth a planet?
questions.explanation: Yes, the earth is a planet. It moves around the sun.
questions.misconception: The earth is not a planet.

questions.stem: Which planet do we live on?
questions.explanation: We live on earth, which is one of the planets in the solar system.

questions.stem: Explain why earth is called a planet.
answer: because it moves around the sun
it orbits the sun like the other planets
it is a body that travels around the sun
hints: What does earth do around the sun?
It is not a star or a satellite.
questions.explanation: Earth is called a planet because it moves around the sun in an orbit, just like the other planets.

questions.stem: What is the moon?
questions.explanation: The moon is a satellite of the earth. It moves around the earth.

questions.stem: What does the moon move around?
hints: It is our nearest neighbour in space.
questions.explanation: The moon moves around the earth. It is a satellite of the earth.
questions.misconception: The moon moves around the sun.

questions.stem: What is a satellite?
answer: a body that moves around a planet
an object that orbits a planet
a smaller body that moves around a larger one like a planet
questions.explanation: A satellite is a body that moves around a planet. The moon is a natural satellite of the earth.

questions.stem: Which of these is a natural satellite of the earth?
hints: It is not made by humans.
questions.explanation: The moon is a natural satellite of the earth. It was not made by humans.

questions.stem: Which planet is closest to the sun?
hints: It is the first planet from the sun.
questions.explanation: Mercury is the closest planet to the sun.
questions.misconception: Earth is the closest planet to the sun.

questions.stem: List the first four planets from the sun in order.
questions.explanation: The first four planets from the sun are Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars.

questions.stem: Which sequence correctly shows the order of the first four planets from the sun?
hints: Mercury is closest to the sun.
questions.explanation: The correct order from the sun is Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars.
questions.misconception: Venus is closer to the sun than Mercury.

indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B5.3.3.1 Show understanding of ecosystem, interdependency of organisms in an ecosystem and appreciate the interactions
indicator.objective: Know how various organisms are adapted to survive in their habitat

questions.stem: What is a habitat?
options: The natural home of a plant or animal
questions.explanation: A habitat is the natural home of a plant or animal.
questions.misconception: A habitat is just any place.

questions.stem: Which of these best describes a habitat?
options: A place where an organism lives naturally
A place where people go to shop
hints: It is about where living things live.
questions.explanation: A habitat is the natural home where an organism lives.

questions.stem: What is a habitat?
answer: the natural home of a plant or animal
the home of a living thing
questions.explanation: A habitat is the natural home of a plant or animal.
questions.misconception: A habitat is just any place.

questions.stem: Which of these is a habitat for fish?
questions.explanation: Water is the habitat for fish. They are adapted to live in water.

questions.stem: Which of these is a habitat for a bird?
questions.explanation: Trees are a common habitat for many birds.

questions.stem: Name two examples of habitats.
hints: One is wet, one is dry.
questions.explanation: Examples of habitats include water, land, trees and soil.

questions.stem: What does adaptation mean?
options: Features that help an organism survive in its habitat
hints: It helps the organism live in its home.
questions.explanation: Adaptation means the features that help an organism survive in its habitat.
questions.misconception: Adaptation means the animal changes its body instantly.

questions.stem: Which statement best explains adaptation?
options: Adaptation is a feature that helps a living thing survive in its habitat
Adaptation is when an animal changes colour for fun
Adaptation is the food an animal eats
Adaptation is the sound an animal makes
hints: It helps the organism live in its home.
questions.explanation: Adaptation is a feature that helps a living thing survive in its habitat.
questions.misconception: Adaptation is not related to survival.

questions.stem: What is adaptation?
answer: features that help an organism survive in its habitat
special features that help living things survive
characteristics that help organisms live in their environment
questions.explanation: Adaptation refers to features that help an organism survive in its habitat.
questions.misconception: Adaptation means the animal changes instantly.

questions.stem: How is a fish adapted to live in water?
options: It has gills to breathe in water and fins to swim
It has lungs to breathe air
questions.explanation: Fish are adapted to water with gills for breathing and fins for swimming.
questions.misconception: Fish have lungs for breathing air.

questions.stem: How is a camel adapted to live in a dry desert?
options: It has a hump that stores fat for energy
hints: The hump helps it survive without much food and water.
questions.explanation: A camel has a hump that stores fat, helping it survive in dry desert conditions.

questions.stem: Describe one adaptation that helps a bird survive in its habitat.
answer: wings for flying to find food
questions.explanation: Birds have wings for flying, which helps them find food and escape danger.

questions.stem: A fish is taken out of water and placed on land. It soon dies. Why?
options: It cannot get oxygen from the air using its gills
It does not like the colour of the ground
hints: Fish use gills to breathe in water.
Gills do not work well in air.
questions.explanation: Fish are adapted to breathe oxygen dissolved in water using gills. On land, their gills cannot get enough oxygen from the air, so they die.

questions.stem: How is a cactus adapted to live in a dry area?
options: It has spines instead of leaves to reduce water loss
It has large flat leaves to catch sunlight
It has many roots that grow above the ground
questions.explanation: A cactus has spines instead of leaves, which reduces water loss and helps it survive in dry areas.

questions.stem: Describe one adaptation that helps a water lily survive in water.
answer: it has flat leaves that float on water
its leaves float on the water surface
it has long stems that reach the surface
questions.explanation: Water lilies have flat leaves that float on the water surface, helping them get sunlight.

questions.stem: Draw a simple diagram of a cactus and a water lily. Label one adaptation of each that helps it survive in its habitat. Write one sentence explaining each adaptation.

criteria.description: Drew a recognizable cactus and water lily
Labeled one adaptation of the cactus (e.g. spines)
Labeled one adaptation of the water lily (e.g. flat floating leaves)
Explained how the cactus adaptation helps it survive
Explained how the water lily adaptation helps it survive

hints: Cacti have spines and thick stems.
Water lilies have flat leaves that float.
questions.explanation: This is a drawing task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.
questions.misconception: Plants do not need to adapt.

questions.stem: Why is adaptation important for animals?
options: It helps them survive in their habitat
hints: Think about finding food and escaping danger.
questions.explanation: Adaptation is important because it helps animals survive in their habitat.

questions.stem: A bird has a sharp beak for eating insects. Why is this adaptation important?
options: It helps the bird find and eat food
It helps the bird change colour
hints: A sharp beak helps with food.
questions.explanation: A sharp beak helps the bird catch and eat insects, which is important for its survival.

questions.stem: Why do living things need adaptations?
answer: to find food and escape danger
to live successfully in their environment
questions.explanation: Living things need adaptations to survive in their habitat, find food and escape danger.

questions.stem: In groups, design and make a simple model of a habitat for a named animal (e.g. fish in a pond, bird in a tree). Your model should show at least two features that help the animal survive in that habitat. Present your model to the class and explain the adaptations.

criteria.description: Designed a model of a habitat for a named animal
Showed at least two features that help the animal survive
Explained the adaptations clearly to the class

hints: Choose an animal and its habitat.
Think about what helps it live there (e.g. gills, wings, roots).
questions.explanation: This is a practical task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.
questions.misconception: All animals can live in any habitat.

indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B5.4.1.1 Demonstrate understanding of the concept of energy, its various forms and sources and the ways in which it can be transformed and conserved
indicator.objective: Explain how energy is transformed from one form to another

questions.stem: Which of these is a form of energy?
hints: Think about what the sun gives.
questions.explanation: Light is a form of energy. Other forms include heat, sound, electrical and mechanical energy.

questions.stem: What form of energy does a radio produce?
questions.explanation: A radio produces sound energy.
questions.misconception: Sound is not a form of energy.

questions.stem: What form of energy does a bulb give out?
hints: It helps you see in the dark.
questions.explanation: A bulb gives out light energy.

questions.stem: What form of energy does a moving car have?
hints: Movement is a form of energy.
questions.explanation: A moving car has mechanical (movement) energy.
questions.misconception: Moving objects do not have energy.

questions.stem: What does energy transformation mean?
options: Energy changing from one form to another
hints: Think about a torch: electrical to light.
questions.explanation: Energy transformation means energy changing from one form to another.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes energy transformation?
options: Energy changes from one form to another
Energy stays in the same form
questions.explanation: Energy transformation is the change of energy from one form to another.

questions.stem: What is energy transformation?
answer: energy changing from one form to another
the change of energy from one form to another
questions.explanation: Energy transformation is the change of energy from one form to another.

questions.stem: A torch uses a battery. What energy transformation happens?
questions.explanation: In a torch, electrical energy from the battery is transformed into light energy.
questions.misconception: A torch creates light without energy.

questions.stem: What energy transformation happens when you ring an electric bell?
questions.explanation: An electric bell transforms electrical energy into sound energy.
questions.misconception: Sound is not a form of energy.

questions.stem: What energy transformation happens when you use an electric iron?
questions.explanation: An electric iron transforms electrical energy into heat energy.

questions.stem: A radio is connected to a battery. Which energy transformation happens?
questions.explanation: A radio transforms electrical energy into sound energy.

questions.stem: Which of these correctly shows an energy transformation?
questions.explanation: A bulb changes electrical energy into light energy.
questions.misconception: Energy transformations are reversed for devices.

questions.stem: Which energy chain correctly shows how energy from the sun reaches a person walking?
hints: Plants use sunlight to make food.
questions.explanation: Energy flows from the sun to plants, then to food, and then to human movement.
questions.misconception: Energy does not come from the sun.

questions.stem: A cow eats grass and then walks. Trace the energy flow.
hints: The grass uses sunlight, and the cow eats the grass.
questions.explanation: The sun gives energy to grass, the cow eats the grass, and the cow uses the energy to move.
questions.misconception: Energy does not come from the sun.

questions.stem: Trace a simple energy chain from the sun to a bird flying.
answer: sun to plant to insect to bird to movement
sun gives energy to plants, insects eat plants, birds eat insects, birds fly
hints: Birds eat insects that eat plants.
questions.explanation: The sun gives energy to plants, insects eat plants, birds eat insects, and the birds use the energy to fly.
questions.misconception: Energy does not flow through food chains.

questions.stem: Draw a simple flow chart to show how energy from the sun can be transformed into movement in a person. Use arrows to show the energy flow.

criteria.description: Started the flow chart with the sun
Included a plant or food in the chain
Included a person in the chain
Ended with movement in the person
Used arrows to show the energy flow

questions.explanation: This is a drawing task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.
questions.misconception: Energy does not come from the sun.

questions.stem: Which energy transformation happens when a gong-gong is beaten at school?
hints: You use your hand to hit it.
questions.explanation: Beating a gong-gong transforms mechanical energy (from your hand) into sound energy.
questions.misconception: Sound is not a form of energy.

questions.stem: Which of these is an example of energy transformation at school?
options: Ringing an electric bell: electrical → sound
questions.explanation: An electric bell transforms electrical energy into sound energy.
questions.misconception: Energy transformation only happens in machines.

questions.stem: Describe one energy transformation that happens at school.
answer: ringing an electric bell: electrical to sound
switching on a bulb: electrical to light
hints: Think about a bell or a bulb.
What energy goes in and what comes out?
questions.explanation: At school, an electric bell transforms electrical energy into sound energy.
questions.misconception: Energy does not change form at school.

questions.stem: Why is energy transformation important for devices like torches and radios?
options: It makes devices work by changing energy into the form they need
It has no effect on devices
questions.explanation: Energy transformation is important because it changes energy into the form needed to make devices work, like a torch producing light.

indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B5.4.1.2 Show understanding of the concept of heat energy in terms of its importance, effects, sources and transfer from one medium to another
indicator.objective: Show the relationship between heat and temperature

questions.stem: What is heat?
options: A form of energy that makes things warm or hot
hints: Think about what the sun gives.
questions.explanation: Heat is a form of energy that makes things warm or hot.
questions.misconception: Heat is not a form of energy.

questions.stem: Which of these best describes heat?
options: The flow of energy from a hotter object to a cooler one
The amount of matter in an object
hints: Heat moves from hot to cold.
It is a form of energy.
questions.explanation: Heat is the flow of energy from a hotter object to a cooler one.
questions.misconception: Heat is not related to energy flow.

questions.stem: Explain what heat is.
answer: a form of energy that makes things warm or hot
heat is a form of energy
questions.explanation: Heat is a form of energy that makes things warm or hot.
questions.misconception: Heat is not a form of energy.

questions.stem: What is temperature?
options: The degree of hotness or coldness of a body
The amount of heat in a body
hints: It tells you how hot or cold something is.
It is measured with a thermometer.
questions.explanation: Temperature is the degree of hotness or coldness of a body.
questions.misconception: Temperature is the same as heat.

questions.stem: Which instrument is used to measure temperature?
hints: It measures how hot or cold something is.
Doctors use it to check for fever.
questions.explanation: A thermometer is used to measure temperature.
questions.misconception: Temperature is measured with a ruler.

questions.stem: What does temperature measure?
answer: the degree of hotness or coldness of a body
how hot or cold something is
the hotness or coldness of an object
hints: It tells you the degree of hotness.
questions.explanation: Temperature measures the degree of hotness or coldness of a body.
questions.misconception: Temperature measures the amount of heat.

questions.stem: When heat is added to a substance, what happens to its temperature?
questions.explanation: When heat is added to a substance, its temperature increases.

questions.stem: When a substance loses heat, what happens to its temperature?
questions.explanation: When a substance loses heat, its temperature decreases.

questions.stem: A stone is placed in the sun. After some time, it feels hot. Why?
options: It gained heat from the sun
It lost heat to the sun
It gained cold from the sun
questions.explanation: The stone gained heat from the sun, so its temperature increased and it feels hot.

questions.stem: In groups, plan and carry out a simple experiment to show that heat changes the temperature of a substance. Describe what you did and what you observed.

criteria.description: Planned a simple experiment involving heating or cooling a substance
Observed and recorded the change in temperature
Explained that heat gained or lost caused the temperature change

hints: You could heat water and measure its temperature.
Or place a stone in the sun and feel it.
questions.explanation: This is a practical task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.

questions.stem: In which direction does heat flow?
options: From a hotter object to a cooler object
From a cooler object to a hotter object
From a smaller object to a larger object
From a lighter object to a heavier object
questions.explanation: Heat flows from a hotter object to a cooler object.
questions.misconception: Heat flows from cold to hot.

questions.stem: A metal spoon is placed in a cup of hot tea. What happens to the spoon?
options: It gains heat from the tea
It loses heat to the tea
questions.explanation: The metal spoon gains heat from the hot tea because heat flows from the hotter tea to the cooler spoon.
questions.misconception: The spoon gives heat to the tea.

questions.stem: Why does a metal spoon left in hot tea become hot after some time?
options: Heat is transferred from the tea to the spoon
The spoon generates its own heat
The tea absorbs cold from the spoon
The spoon absorbs light from the tea
hints: Heat moves from hot to cold.
The tea is hotter than the spoon.
questions.explanation: Heat is transferred from the hot tea to the cooler spoon, making the spoon hot.
questions.misconception: The spoon produces heat on its own.

questions.stem: Explain how heat is transferred from a hot object to a cooler object.
answer: heat flows from the hotter object to the cooler object until both reach the same temperature
heat moves from hot to cold
heat transfers from the hotter object to the cooler one
hints: Think about hot tea and a cold spoon.
questions.explanation: Heat flows from a hotter object to a cooler object until both reach the same temperature.
questions.misconception: Heat flows from cold to hot.

questions.stem: Which of these is an example of heat affecting temperature?
options: A stone becoming hot in the sun
questions.explanation: A stone becoming hot in the sun is an example of heat affecting temperature.

questions.stem: When you put water in a fridge, what happens to its temperature?
questions.explanation: When water is put in a fridge, it loses heat, so its temperature decreases.
questions.misconception: The fridge adds heat to the water.

questions.stem: Give one example of heat affecting temperature in everyday life.
answer: putting water in a fridge makes it colder
a stone left in the sun becomes hot
heating water on a fire increases its temperature
an ice cube melts in the sun
hints: Think about something getting hot or cold.
The sun or a fridge can cause changes.
questions.explanation: An example is putting water in a fridge, which makes it colder as it loses heat.
questions.misconception: Heat does not affect everyday objects.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes heat and temperature?
options: Heat is a form of energy, while temperature is a measure of hotness
Heat is a measure of hotness, while temperature is a form of energy
Heat and temperature are the same thing
Heat is measured in degrees, while temperature is measured in joules
hints: Temperature tells you how hot or cold something is.
questions.explanation: Heat is a form of energy, while temperature is a measure of the degree of hotness or coldness.
questions.misconception: Heat and temperature are the same.

questions.stem: A large bucket of warm water and a small cup of boiling water are compared. Which statement is true?
options: The boiling water has a higher temperature, but the bucket may contain more heat
The bucket has a higher temperature
hints: Heat depends on the amount of substance too.
questions.explanation: The boiling water has a higher temperature because it is boiling, but the large bucket of warm water may contain more total heat because it has more water.
questions.misconception: A larger object always has a higher temperature.

questions.stem: Explain the difference between heat and temperature.
answer: heat is a form of energy, while temperature is a measure of the degree of hotness or coldness
heat is energy, temperature is how hot or cold something is
heat is energy that flows, temperature is a measure of hotness
hints: Temperature tells you hot or cold.
questions.explanation: Heat is a form of energy that flows from hot to cold, while temperature is a measure of how hot or cold an object is.
questions.misconception: Heat and temperature are the same thing.

indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B5.4.1.2 Show understanding of the concept of heat energy in terms of its importance, effects, sources and transfer from one medium to another
indicator.objective: Measure and record temperature using thermometer

questions.stem: Which instrument is used to measure temperature?
hints: Doctors use it to check for fever.
It measures how hot or cold something is.
questions.explanation: A thermometer is used to measure temperature.
questions.misconception: Temperature is measured with a ruler.

questions.stem: A learner wants to measure the temperature of warm water. Which instrument should they use?
hints: Temperature is measured with a special instrument.
It has a scale marked in degrees.
questions.explanation: A thermometer is used to measure the temperature of warm water.
questions.misconception: Temperature can be measured with a ruler.

questions.stem: What instrument is used to measure temperature?
questions.explanation: A thermometer is used to measure temperature.
questions.misconception: Temperature is measured with a scale.

questions.stem: Which thermometer is used to measure body temperature?
questions.explanation: A clinical thermometer is used to measure body temperature.
questions.misconception: Clinical thermometers measure the temperature of liquids in the lab.

questions.stem: Which thermometer is used in a science laboratory to measure the temperature of liquids?
hints: It is used in science experiments.
questions.explanation: A laboratory thermometer is used to measure the temperature of liquids in a laboratory.
questions.misconception: Clinical thermometers are used for laboratory liquids.

questions.stem: Name one type of thermometer and state what it is used for.
answer: laboratory thermometer: measuring temperature of liquids
hints: One is used in science labs.
questions.explanation: A clinical thermometer is used for body temperature. A laboratory thermometer is used for measuring the temperature of liquids.

questions.stem: What is the normal body temperature of a healthy person?
hints: It is close to 37 degrees Celsius.
questions.explanation: The normal body temperature of a healthy person is about 37°C.

questions.stem: At what temperature does water boil?
hints: It is much higher than body temperature.
questions.explanation: Water boils at 100°C.

questions.stem: A thermometer reads 39°C for a sick learner. What does this show?
questions.explanation: A body temperature of 39°C is higher than normal (37°C), showing the learner has a fever.

questions.stem: A thermometer shows a reading of 37°C. What does this temperature represent?
answer: the normal body temperature of a healthy person
hints: It is the temperature of a healthy person.
questions.explanation: 37°C represents the normal body temperature of a healthy person.
questions.misconception: 37°C means the person has a fever.

questions.stem: Which is the correct way to record a temperature reading?
hints: Temperature is measured in degrees Celsius.
questions.explanation: Temperature is recorded in degrees Celsius (°C). So 37°C is correct.

questions.stem: Record the following temperature reading: thirty-seven degrees Celsius.
questions.explanation: Thirty-seven degrees Celsius is written as 37°C.

questions.stem: A learner measures the temperature of warm water and gets 45 degrees Celsius. Write this reading correctly with its unit.
questions.explanation: The reading is written as 45°C.

questions.stem: Before using a clinical thermometer, what should you do first?
hints: It must be clean before use.
questions.explanation: A clinical thermometer should be cleaned before use to keep it safe and hygienic.

questions.stem: How long should a clinical thermometer be left in place before reading the temperature?
hints: It takes a short time for the reading to settle.
questions.explanation: A clinical thermometer should be left in place for a few minutes before reading the temperature.

questions.stem: Describe one safety step when using a clinical thermometer.
answer: clean it before and after use
do not heat it in fire
handle it carefully so it does not break
questions.explanation: One safety step is to clean the thermometer before and after use. It should also be handled carefully to avoid breaking.
questions.misconception: Thermometers can be heated in fire.

questions.stem: In groups, use a clinical thermometer (or a model) to measure body temperature and a laboratory thermometer to measure the temperature of warm water. Record your readings. Describe what you did and what you found.

criteria.description: Used the clinical thermometer correctly to measure body temperature
Used the laboratory thermometer correctly to measure warm water
Recorded both readings with correct units (°C)

hints: Wait a few minutes before reading.
questions.explanation: This is a practical task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.
questions.misconception: Clinical and laboratory thermometers can be used interchangeably.

questions.stem: Why is it important to measure body temperature when someone is sick?
hints: A high temperature can be a sign of sickness.
questions.explanation: Measuring body temperature helps check for fever, which can be a sign of illness.

questions.stem: Give one reason why measuring temperature is important.
answer: to know if water is hot enough
to know how hot or cold something is
questions.explanation: Measuring temperature is important to check for fever, to know if water is safe to boil, and to monitor health.

questions.stem: A nurse measures a patient's temperature and finds it is 40°C. What does this indicate?
options: The patient has a high fever and needs attention
questions.explanation: A temperature of 40°C is much higher than normal body temperature (37°C), indicating a high fever that needs medical attention.

indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B5.4.2.1 Demonstrate knowledge of generation of electricity, its transmission and transformation into other forms
indicator.objective: Identify the components of an electric circuit and their functions

questions.stem: Which of these is a basic component of an electric circuit?
hints: Which one stores energy for the circuit?
It has two ends, positive and negative.
questions.explanation: A battery is a basic component of an electric circuit. It supplies energy to make the circuit work.
questions.misconception: The battery is not part of the circuit.

questions.stem: Which set lists only basic components of an electric circuit?
hints: Which set has parts used in a real circuit?
A switch, bulb, wire and battery all belong in a circuit.
questions.explanation: The basic components of an electric circuit are the battery, bulb, connecting wire and switch.
questions.misconception: Any object can be part of an electric circuit.

questions.stem: Name two basic components of an electric circuit.
questions.explanation: Two basic components are the battery and the bulb. Other components include the switch and connecting wires.
questions.misconception: Only the bulb matters in a circuit.

questions.stem: A pupil lists four items: battery, wire, switch, bulb. Which of these is NOT a basic component of an electric circuit?
hints: Which one is not used to make a simple circuit?
A magnet is not part of a simple circuit.
questions.explanation: A magnet is not a basic component of an electric circuit. The basic components are battery, wire, switch and bulb.
questions.misconception: Any object can be used in a circuit.

questions.stem: What is the function of the battery in an electric circuit?
options: It opens and closes the circuit
questions.explanation: The battery supplies energy to the circuit. This energy makes the bulb light and the components work.

questions.stem: What is the function of the switch in an electric circuit?
options: It opens and closes the circuit
hints: A switch can be on or off.
questions.explanation: The switch opens and closes the circuit. When the switch is closed, electricity flows; when open, the circuit is broken.
questions.misconception: A switch is not needed in a circuit.

questions.stem: What is the function of the connecting wire in an electric circuit?
answer: it carries electricity around the circuit
questions.explanation: The connecting wire carries electricity around the circuit, linking the battery, switch and bulb.
questions.misconception: Wires are not important in a circuit.

questions.stem: Match the component to its function. Which pair is correct?
options: Wire → opens and closes the circuit
hints: Think about what each part does.
questions.explanation: The battery supplies energy. The bulb gives light, the switch opens/closes the circuit, and the wire carries electricity.

questions.stem: When will a bulb in a simple circuit light up?
hints: A complete circuit lets electricity flow.
questions.explanation: A bulb lights up only when the circuit is complete, allowing electricity to flow through it.
questions.misconception: A bulb lights even if the circuit is broken.

questions.stem: What happens if the connecting wire in a circuit is cut?
questions.explanation: If the wire is cut, the circuit is broken. Electricity cannot flow, so the bulb does not light.
questions.misconception: A bulb lights even with a broken wire.

questions.stem: A pupil connects a battery, wire and bulb, but the bulb does not light. What is the most likely reason?
questions.explanation: The most likely reason is that the circuit is not complete. A loose connection or a gap in the circuit stops electricity from flowing.
questions.misconception: The bulb lights even if the circuit is broken.

questions.stem: A pupil wants to make a simple circuit but has no dry cell. Which of these can be used instead to supply energy?
hints: A lemon can act as a simple battery.
questions.explanation: A lemon can be used as a simple battery to supply energy in a circuit.
questions.misconception: Only dry cells can supply energy.

questions.stem: Name one material that can be used as a connecting wire in an emergency.
hints: It must be a metal that conducts electricity.
Think of something thin and metallic.
questions.explanation: Materials like aluminium foil, paper clips, or metal spoons can be used as connecting wires because they conduct electricity.

questions.stem: A pupil wants to make a simple circuit but has no switch. What can they use instead to open and close the circuit?
hints: The switch needs to conduct electricity when closed.
A metal paper clip can be bent to make or break contact.
questions.explanation: A metal paper clip can be used as a simple switch because it conducts electricity and can be moved to open or close the circuit.
questions.misconception: Any material can be used as a switch.

questions.stem: Draw a simple electric circuit with a battery, a bulb, and connecting wires.

criteria.description: Drew a battery in the circuit
Drew a bulb in the circuit
Drew connecting wires linking the components
The drawing forms a complete loop (closed circuit)

hints: Connect the bulb to the battery with wires.
questions.explanation: This is a drawing task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.
questions.misconception: The circuit does not need to form a complete loop.

questions.stem: Draw a simple circuit that includes a battery, a switch, a bulb and connecting wires. Label all four components.

criteria.description: Drew a battery and labeled it
Drew a switch and labeled it
Drew a bulb and labeled it
Drew connecting wires and labeled them
The components form a complete closed loop

questions.explanation: This is a drawing task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.
questions.misconception: Some components can be left out of the drawing.

questions.stem: Draw a circuit diagram using symbols for a battery, a switch and a bulb. Show the switch in the open position and in the closed position.

criteria.description: Used correct symbols for battery, switch and bulb
Drew the switch in the open position
Drew the switch in the closed position
Both diagrams form complete loops (except at the open switch)

hints: Use simple symbols for each component.
Open switch = gap in the circuit.
questions.explanation: This is a drawing task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.
questions.misconception: Open and closed switches look the same in a diagram.

questions.stem: In groups, use a battery, connecting wires and a bulb. Connect them to make the bulb light. Show your working circuit to your teacher.

criteria.description: Connected the battery, wires and bulb correctly
Worked safely and cooperatively in the group

hints: Make sure all connections are tight.
The circuit must be complete for the bulb to light.
questions.explanation: This is a practical task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.
questions.misconception: The bulb can light even if the circuit is not complete.

questions.stem: In groups, build a circuit with a battery, wire, switch and bulb. Show how the switch turns the bulb on and off.

criteria.description: Built a circuit with battery, wire, switch and bulb
Showed the bulb lighting when the switch is closed
Showed the bulb going off when the switch is open

hints: Close the switch to let electricity flow.
questions.explanation: This is a practical task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.
questions.misconception: The switch is not needed in a circuit.

questions.stem: In groups, build a circuit with a battery, wire and bulb. Test different materials (e.g. a metal spoon, a plastic ruler, a piece of paper) by placing them in the circuit. Record which materials let the bulb light and which do not.

criteria.description: Built a working circuit with battery, wire and bulb
Tested at least three different materials
Correctly recorded which materials let the bulb light (conductors)
Correctly recorded which materials did not let the bulb light (insulators)

hints: Plastics and paper usually do not.
questions.explanation: This is a practical task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.

indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B5.4.3.1 Know that movement is caused by applied forces due to the release of stored energy
indicator.objective: Explain the term, 'friction', its effects and applications

questions.stem: What is friction?
options: A force that helps objects move faster
A force that opposes movement between two surfaces
hints: Think about rubbing your hands together.
questions.explanation: Friction is a force that opposes the movement of two surfaces against each other.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes friction?
options: A force that pulls objects towards the earth
A force that opposes the movement of two surfaces against each other
A force that makes objects float
hints: It acts when surfaces rub together.
questions.explanation: Friction is the force that opposes the movement of two surfaces against each other.
questions.misconception: Friction is a pulling force like gravity.

questions.stem: What is friction?
answer: a force that opposes movement between two surfaces
the force that opposes the movement of two surfaces against each other
a force that slows down movement
questions.explanation: Friction is the force that opposes the movement of two surfaces against each other.

questions.stem: A pupil says, 'Friction only happens when things move fast.' What is the best correction?
options: Yes, friction only happens at high speed
No, friction happens whenever two surfaces rub together, even at low speed
No, friction only happens in water
No, friction only happens in machines
hints: Think about slowly sliding a book on a table.
Friction acts whenever surfaces touch and move.
questions.explanation: Friction happens whenever two surfaces rub together, even if the movement is slow.
questions.misconception: Friction only happens when things move fast.

questions.stem: What happens when you rub your palms together?
hints: Think about the heat you feel.
questions.explanation: Rubbing your palms together produces heat due to friction, so they become warm.

questions.stem: Which of these is an effect of friction?
questions.explanation: Friction produces heat when surfaces rub together.

questions.stem: Why do the soles of shoes wear out over time?
options: Because of friction between the shoes and the ground
hints: Think about walking on rough surfaces.
questions.explanation: Friction between the soles of shoes and the ground causes the soles to wear out over time.
questions.misconception: Shoes wear out because they get wet.

questions.stem: Describe one effect of friction.
questions.explanation: Friction produces heat, slows down movement, and causes wear and tear.

questions.stem: Which of these is an example of friction?
hints: Which action involves surfaces rubbing together?
Your hands rub against each other.
questions.explanation: Rubbing your hands together is an example of friction.

questions.stem: A car tyre grips the road as the car moves. What causes this grip?
options: Friction between the tyre and the road
questions.explanation: Friction between the car tyre and the road helps the tyre grip and prevents slipping.

questions.stem: Give one everyday example of friction.
answer: a car tyre on the road
sliding a book on a table
questions.explanation: Examples of friction include rubbing hands together, shoes gripping the ground, and car tyres on the road.

questions.stem: Which of these reduces friction?
options: Increasing the weight on the surfaces
questions.explanation: Applying oil between two surfaces reduces friction, making it easier for them to slide over each other.

questions.stem: Why is water sometimes used on a slide in a playground?
options: To reduce friction so children can slide easily
questions.explanation: Water reduces friction on the slide, allowing children to slide down more easily.

questions.stem: Name one way to reduce friction.
questions.explanation: Ways to reduce friction include using oil or water, or making surfaces smooth.

questions.stem: Which of these increases friction?
questions.explanation: Using a rough surface increases friction between surfaces.

questions.stem: Why do shoes have treads (patterns) on the soles?
options: To increase friction and prevent slipping
questions.explanation: Treads on shoe soles increase friction between the shoe and the ground, helping to prevent slipping.

questions.stem: Explain why car tyres are made with rough patterns on them.
answer: to increase friction between the tyre and the road, helping the car grip and preventing slipping
rough patterns increase friction so the tyres grip the road better
they increase friction to stop the car from slipping
hints: Think about driving on a wet road.
questions.explanation: Car tyres have rough patterns to increase friction between the tyre and the road. This helps the car grip the road and prevents slipping, especially on wet surfaces.

questions.stem: Why is friction useful when walking?
options: It helps our shoes grip the ground and prevents slipping
hints: Think about slipping on a wet floor.
questions.explanation: Friction between our shoes and the ground helps us grip and prevents slipping when walking.
questions.misconception: Friction is not useful for walking.

questions.stem: On a rainy day, why do people sometimes slip on a smooth floor?
options: Because friction is reduced by the water
Because friction is increased by the water
questions.explanation: Water reduces friction between shoes and the floor, so there is less grip and people can slip.

questions.stem: Explain how friction can be both useful and harmful in everyday life.
answer: friction is useful because it helps us walk without slipping and helps tyres grip the road; it is harmful because it causes wear and tear on shoes and machine parts
friction helps with grip but also causes wear
useful for grip; harmful because it causes wearing out
hints: Think about walking and car tyres.
questions.explanation: Friction is useful because it gives grip for walking and driving. It is harmful because it causes wear and tear on shoes, tyres, and machine parts, and produces unwanted heat.

indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B5.5.1.1 Recognise the importance of personal hygiene
indicator.objective: Know why it is important to wash clothes regularly

questions.stem: Why should we wash our clothes regularly?
hints: Think about what collects on clothes when you wear them.
Dirt and sweat make clothes dirty.
questions.explanation: We wash clothes regularly to remove dirt and sweat, keeping them clean and healthy to wear.
questions.misconception: Clothes only need washing when visibly dirty.

questions.stem: Which of these is a reason for washing clothes regularly?
options: To remove germs that can cause sickness
hints: Germs can collect on dirty clothes.
questions.explanation: Washing clothes regularly removes germs that can cause skin problems and sickness.
questions.misconception: Dirty clothes do not cause health problems.

questions.stem: Give one reason why it is important to wash clothes regularly.
answer: to keep clothes clean and healthy
questions.explanation: Washing clothes regularly removes dirt, sweat and germs, and prevents body odour.

questions.stem: Ama wears the same uniform for one week without washing it. What is likely to happen?
options: The uniform will smell and may cause skin irritation
The uniform will change colour to white
hints: Sweat and dirt collect on worn clothes.
Dirty clothes can smell and cause skin problems.
questions.explanation: Wearing unwashed clothes for a week allows sweat and dirt to collect, causing body odour and possible skin irritation.
questions.misconception: Clothes do not need regular washing.

questions.stem: Which materials are needed to wash clothes?
hints: What do you use in a washing basin?
questions.explanation: Soap and water are needed to wash clothes. A basin and brush may also be used.
questions.misconception: Soap is not needed to wash clothes.

questions.stem: Which of these is used to scrub clothes when washing by hand?
hints: It helps remove dirt from the cloth.
questions.explanation: A brush is used to scrub clothes and remove dirt when washing by hand.
questions.misconception: A spoon is used to scrub clothes.

questions.stem: Name two materials needed for washing clothes.
hints: Think about what makes the clothes clean.
One is liquid, one is solid.
questions.explanation: Materials needed for washing clothes include soap, water, a basin and a brush.
questions.misconception: Only water is needed to wash clothes.

questions.stem: What is the correct order for washing clothes by hand?
options: Soak, scrub with soap, rinse, dry
questions.explanation: The correct order is: soak the clothes, scrub with soap, rinse with clean water, then dry in the sun.
questions.misconception: You can dry clothes before rinsing.

questions.stem: Why should clothes be rinsed with clean water after scrubbing with soap?
options: To remove the soap and dirt
hints: Soap can remain on clothes if not rinsed.
questions.explanation: Clothes should be rinsed with clean water to remove soap and dirt, leaving them clean and safe to wear.

questions.stem: Describe the steps for washing clothes by hand.
answer: soak the clothes in water, scrub with soap, rinse with clean water, and dry in the sun
soak, scrub with soap, rinse, and dry
wet the clothes, add soap and scrub, rinse, then dry
questions.explanation: To wash clothes by hand: soak them in water, scrub with soap, rinse with clean water, and dry in the sun.

questions.stem: After washing, why should clothes be dried in the sun?
options: The sun helps kill germs and dries the clothes
The sun makes the clothes wetter
The sun makes the clothes heavier
The sun changes the colour of the clothes
hints: The sun gives heat and light.
questions.explanation: Drying clothes in the sun helps kill germs and removes moisture, keeping the clothes clean and fresh.

questions.stem: What can happen if you wear dirty clothes for a long time?
options: You may get body odour and skin problems
hints: Dirty clothes collect sweat and germs.
This can cause smell and skin irritation.
questions.explanation: Wearing dirty clothes for a long time can cause body odour and skin problems because of sweat and germs.
questions.misconception: Dirty clothes do not cause health problems.

questions.stem: State one consequence of not washing clothes regularly.
questions.explanation: Not washing clothes regularly can cause body odour, skin infections and sickness.

questions.stem: A learner wears dirty socks for several days and develops an itchy rash on the feet. What is the most likely cause?
options: Germs and sweat on the dirty socks
hints: Dirty socks collect sweat and germs.
questions.explanation: Germs and sweat on dirty socks can cause skin irritation and rashes on the feet.
questions.misconception: Dirty socks do not cause skin problems.

questions.stem: Which of these is another method of washing clothes besides hand washing?
hints: It is a machine that washes clothes.
questions.explanation: A washing machine is another method of washing clothes. It uses electricity to wash clothes automatically.
questions.misconception: Hand washing is the only way to wash clothes.

questions.stem: Name one method of washing clothes other than hand washing.
questions.explanation: A washing machine is a method of washing clothes other than hand washing.

questions.stem: A family wants to save time washing clothes. Which method would be fastest?
options: Washing by hand one by one
hints: Which method does most of the work automatically?
A machine can wash many clothes quickly.
questions.explanation: Using a washing machine is the fastest method because it washes many clothes automatically in a short time.

questions.stem: Design a simple weekly roster for washing your clothes. Write the days of the week and what you will wash each day (e.g. Monday: school uniform; Wednesday: socks; Saturday: bedsheets).

criteria.description: Included at least three days of the week
Assigned specific clothes to wash on each day

hints: Think about when you have time to wash.
questions.explanation: This is a written task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.
questions.misconception: A washing roster is not needed.

questions.stem: Why is it helpful to have a roster for washing clothes?
answer: it helps you remember when to wash your clothes regularly
it reminds you to wash clothes on specific days
hints: Think about not forgetting to wash.
questions.explanation: A roster helps you remember to wash your clothes regularly and keeps your washing organised.

questions.stem: A learner washes only underwear every day but other clothes only once a month. What is the best advice?
options: Wash all clothes regularly, not just underwear
Wash clothes only when they smell
hints: All clothes collect sweat and dirt.
Regular washing keeps all clothes clean.
questions.explanation: All clothes should be washed regularly, not just underwear, to prevent dirt, sweat and germs from building up.

indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B5.5.1.2 Identify, discuss and appreciate the natural and human features of the environment and the need to keep the environment clean
indicator.objective: Know how to keep washrooms clean

questions.stem: Why should washrooms be kept clean?
options: To prevent germs and bad smell
hints: Dirty washrooms can smell and have germs.
questions.explanation: Washrooms should be kept clean to prevent germs, bad smell and the spread of disease.

questions.stem: Which of these is a reason for keeping washrooms clean?
options: To stop the spread of diseases
hints: Germs can spread in dirty washrooms.
questions.explanation: Keeping washrooms clean helps stop the spread of diseases.
questions.misconception: A dirty washroom is only a smell problem.

questions.stem: Give one reason why washrooms should be kept clean.
questions.explanation: Washrooms should be kept clean to prevent germs, bad smell and disease.

questions.stem: A dirty washroom can attract flies. Why is this a health risk?
options: Flies can carry germs from the washroom to food and people
Flies make the washroom look pretty
Flies make the washroom smell better
hints: They can carry germs to food.
questions.explanation: Flies attracted to dirty washrooms can carry germs to food and people, spreading disease.

questions.stem: What should you do immediately after using a toilet?
questions.explanation: You should flush the toilet immediately after use to keep it clean and prevent bad smell.

questions.stem: Where should used tissue paper be placed?
hints: It should go into a bin.
questions.explanation: Used tissue paper should be placed in a waste bin to keep the washroom clean.
questions.misconception: Throwing tissue on the floor is acceptable.

questions.stem: State one way to keep a washroom clean.
hints: Think about what you do after using the toilet.
questions.explanation: Ways to keep washrooms clean include flushing after use, putting tissue in the bin, and cleaning regularly.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a good way to keep a washroom clean?
hints: Which action makes the washroom dirty?
Tissue on the floor is not clean.
questions.explanation: Throwing tissue on the floor makes the washroom dirty. The other actions help keep it clean.
questions.misconception: Throwing tissue on the floor is acceptable.

questions.stem: What can happen if a washroom is not kept clean?
options: It can smell bad and spread diseases
questions.explanation: A dirty washroom can smell bad and spread diseases.
questions.misconception: A dirty washroom is only a smell problem.

questions.stem: State one consequence of not keeping a washroom clean.
questions.explanation: Not keeping a washroom clean can cause bad smell, flies and the spread of disease.

questions.stem: A school washroom is not cleaned for many days. What is the most likely health effect on learners?
options: Learners may get sick from germs
hints: Germs build up in dirty places.
questions.explanation: If a washroom is not cleaned for many days, germs build up and learners may get sick.
questions.misconception: Dirty washrooms do not affect health.

questions.stem: What should you do after using a washroom?
options: Wash your hands with soap and water
Wipe your hands on your clothes
questions.explanation: After using a washroom, you should wash your hands with soap and water to remove germs.
questions.misconception: Hand washing after using the washroom is not necessary.

questions.stem: What should you do with the toilet after using it?
questions.explanation: You should flush the toilet after using it to keep it clean.

questions.stem: Which of these is good washroom behaviour?
options: Flushing after use and washing hands
hints: Good behaviour keeps the washroom clean.
questions.explanation: Good washroom behaviour includes flushing after use and washing hands with soap and water.

questions.stem: Design a poster to encourage learners to keep the school washroom clean. Include at least two clear actions (e.g. 'Flush after use', 'Put tissue in the bin') and a short message.

criteria.description: Included at least two correct actions for keeping the washroom clean
Poster is neat and easy to understand

hints: Think about flushing and throwing tissue in the bin.
Write a short message like 'Keep our washroom clean!'
questions.explanation: This is a drawing task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.

questions.stem: Write a short message for a poster encouraging learners to keep the washroom clean.
answer: flush after use and wash your hands
let us keep the washroom clean
questions.explanation: A short message like 'Keep our washroom clean' encourages good habits.

questions.stem: List three rules you would put on a washroom poster to keep it clean.

criteria.description: Listed three clear and correct rules

hints: Think about flushing, tissue disposal, and hand washing.
questions.explanation: This is a written task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.

questions.stem: How can learners help keep school washrooms clean?
options: By flushing after use and putting tissue in the bin
By throwing tissue on the floor
hints: Good habits keep the washroom clean.
questions.explanation: Learners can help by flushing after use, putting tissue in the bin, and washing their hands.
questions.misconception: Learners cannot help keep washrooms clean.

questions.stem: State one way learners can help keep school washrooms clean.
answer: report dirty washrooms to the teacher
questions.explanation: Learners can help by flushing after use, putting tissue in the bin, and reporting problems to the teacher.
questions.misconception: Only adults can keep washrooms clean.

questions.stem: A learner notices that the school washroom is very dirty. What is the best action to take?
options: Tell the teacher so it can be cleaned
Close the washroom and never use it
hints: Tell an adult who can help.
questions.explanation: The best action is to tell the teacher so the washroom can be cleaned and kept healthy for everyone.

indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B5.5.2.1 Know common diseases of humans; causes, symptoms, effects and prevention
indicator.objective: Identify causes, symptoms and prevention of cholera

questions.stem: What causes cholera?
options: Germs from contaminated food or water
hints: Cholera is linked to dirty water.
It is caused by tiny germs.
questions.explanation: Cholera is caused by germs that come from contaminated food or water.
questions.misconception: Cholera is caused by eating too much food.

questions.stem: A learner says, 'Cholera is spread through the air like a cold.' What is the best correction?
options: Yes, cholera spreads through the air
No, cholera spreads mainly through contaminated water and food
No, cholera is caused by malaria
No, cholera cannot spread at all
hints: Think about dirty water and food.
Cholera is not an airborne disease.
questions.explanation: Cholera spreads mainly through drinking contaminated water or eating contaminated food, not through the air.
questions.misconception: Cholera is spread through the air.

questions.stem: What causes cholera?
answer: germs from contaminated food or water
questions.explanation: Cholera is caused by germs found in contaminated food or water.
questions.misconception: Cholera is caused by bad air.

questions.stem: Which of these is a common symptom of cholera?
hints: Cholera affects the stomach and toilet habits.
questions.explanation: Serious diarrhoea is a common symptom of cholera.

questions.stem: Which set lists common symptoms of cholera?
hints: Cholera causes watery stool and vomiting.
The body loses a lot of water.
questions.explanation: Common symptoms of cholera include diarrhoea, vomiting and dehydration.

questions.stem: Name two symptoms of cholera.
questions.explanation: Common symptoms of cholera are diarrhoea and vomiting. Dehydration also occurs.

questions.stem: Why is dehydration dangerous for a person with cholera?
options: The body loses too much water and salts
The body gains too much water
The body produces too much blood
hints: Diarrhoea and vomiting remove water from the body.
The body needs water to function.
questions.explanation: Dehydration is dangerous because the body loses too much water and salts, which can lead to serious health problems.

questions.stem: How can cholera spread from one person to another?
hints: Cholera germs are in dirty water.
People get it from what they eat or drink.
questions.explanation: Cholera spreads when people drink contaminated water or eat contaminated food.

questions.stem: Which of these can help cholera spread?
options: Drinking water from a dirty stream
Covering food with a clean cloth
hints: Which action brings germs into the body?
questions.explanation: Drinking water from a dirty stream can spread cholera because the water contains germs.
questions.misconception: Cholera is not spread by water.

questions.stem: Describe one way cholera can spread.
answer: drinking water from a dirty source
hints: Think about food that flies have touched.
questions.explanation: Cholera can spread through drinking contaminated water or eating contaminated food.

questions.stem: Which of these helps prevent cholera?
hints: Safe water is free from germs.
questions.explanation: Drinking safe water helps prevent cholera because it does not contain cholera germs.
questions.misconception: Any water is safe to drink.

questions.stem: Which of these is a good way to prevent cholera?
options: Washing hands with soap before eating
Eating food that has been left uncovered
questions.explanation: Washing hands with soap before eating helps prevent cholera by removing germs.

questions.stem: Give one way to prevent cholera.
questions.explanation: Ways to prevent cholera include drinking safe water, washing hands with soap, and covering food.

questions.stem: A family collects water from a river. What should they do to make it safe to drink?
options: Let the water settle and drink it
hints: River water can contain cholera germs.
questions.explanation: Boiling river water kills cholera germs and makes it safe to drink.

questions.stem: A learner has serious diarrhoea and vomiting. What should you do?
options: Tell an adult and take the learner to a health worker
questions.explanation: You should tell an adult and take the learner to a health worker immediately.
questions.misconception: Cholera does not need medical help.

questions.stem: What should you do if someone shows signs of cholera?
answer: give them safe water and take them to a health worker
tell an adult and see a health worker
give safe water and seek medical help
questions.explanation: Give the person safe water to drink and take them to a health worker immediately.
questions.misconception: You should wait for cholera to go away.

questions.stem: A cholera patient is very thirsty and weak. What is the most important first step?
options: Give them safe water to drink
questions.explanation: Giving safe water is the most important first step to replace lost fluids and prevent severe dehydration.
questions.misconception: Cholera patients should not drink water.

questions.stem: Draw a simple table with three columns: 'Causes', 'Symptoms' and 'Prevention'. Write at least one correct point under each column for cholera.

criteria.description: Wrote one correct cause of cholera
Wrote one correct symptom of cholera
Wrote one correct way to prevent cholera
Organised the points clearly under the three headings

hints: Think about dirty water for causes.
Think about boiling water for prevention.
questions.explanation: This is a written task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.
questions.misconception: Cholera has no clear causes or prevention.

questions.stem: Design a simple poster to teach your class about cholera. Show one cause, one symptom and one way to prevent it. Use drawings and short words.

criteria.description: Showed one correct cause of cholera
Showed one correct symptom of cholera
Showed one correct way to prevent cholera
Used drawings and short words clearly

hints: Draw dirty water for a cause.
Draw a sick person for a symptom.
Draw soap and water for prevention.
questions.explanation: This is a drawing task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.

questions.stem: Complete this sentence: Cholera is caused by ______ and can be prevented by ______.
answer: germs from contaminated water, drinking safe water
germs in dirty water, washing hands
contaminated food and water, boiling water
hints: Second blank: how to stop it?
questions.explanation: Cholera is caused by germs from contaminated water or food and can be prevented by drinking safe water and washing hands.
questions.misconception: Cholera has no cause or prevention.

indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B5.5.3.1 Recognise the impact of science and technology in society
indicator.objective: Identify the raw materials used in some local industries (kenkey production, gari production, ceramic and pottery production)

questions.stem: Which raw material is used to make kenkey?
hints: Kenkey is a food made from a common cereal.
It is not made from cassava.
questions.explanation: Kenkey is made from maize. The maize is ground and fermented to make the dough.

questions.stem: Which raw material is used to make gari?
hints: Gari is made from a root crop.
It is not made from maize.
questions.explanation: Gari is made from cassava. The cassava is grated, pressed, and fried.

questions.stem: Which raw material is used in pottery production?
hints: Pots are made from a material that can be moulded when wet.
It is found in the ground.
questions.explanation: Clay is the raw material used in pottery. It can be moulded and then baked to make pots and bowls.

questions.stem: Name the raw material used to make kenkey.
questions.explanation: Maize is the raw material used to make kenkey.

questions.stem: Which pair correctly matches a product to its raw material?
questions.explanation: Kenkey is made from maize. Gari is made from cassava, and pots are made from clay.

questions.stem: A learner wants to make gari. Which raw material should they gather?
questions.explanation: To make gari, the learner needs cassava. Cassava is processed into gari.

questions.stem: Match the product to its raw material: kenkey, gari, pot.
answer: kenkey - maize, gari - cassava, pot - clay
kenkey: maize; gari: cassava; pot: clay
questions.explanation: Kenkey is made from maize, gari from cassava, and pots from clay.
questions.misconception: All products use the same raw material.

questions.stem: Which set correctly matches three local products to their raw materials?
options: Kenkey → maize; gari → cassava; pot → clay
Kenkey → cassava; gari → maize; pot → wood
Kenkey → clay; gari → maize; pot → cassava
Kenkey → maize; gari → clay; pot → cassava
hints: Think about the main ingredient for each product.
Kenkey is maize-based, gari is cassava-based, and pots are clay-based.
questions.explanation: The correct matching is: kenkey → maize; gari → cassava; pot → clay.

questions.stem: How is cassava changed into gari?
hints: Gari is a dry, granular food.
The cassava is grated and fried.
questions.explanation: Cassava is grated, pressed to remove water, and then fried to make gari.
questions.misconception: Gari is made by boiling cassava.

questions.stem: How is clay changed into a pot?
options: Moulded and baked in a fire
hints: It is then heated to make it hard.
questions.explanation: Clay is moulded into shape and then baked in a fire to make a pot.
questions.misconception: Clay is boiled to make a pot.

questions.stem: Describe one step in making gari from cassava.
answer: the cassava is fried after grating
hints: It is grated into small pieces.
questions.explanation: One step in making gari is grating the cassava. The grated cassava is then pressed and fried.
questions.misconception: Gari is made without processing cassava.

questions.stem: Describe how maize is changed into kenkey.
answer: the maize is ground into flour, mixed with water, fermented, and cooked
maize is ground and fermented then cooked
questions.explanation: Maize is ground into flour, mixed with water, left to ferment, and then cooked to make kenkey.
questions.misconception: Kenkey is made from unprocessed maize.

questions.stem: Why are local industries like kenkey production important?
questions.explanation: Local industries like kenkey production are important because they provide food and create jobs for people.

questions.stem: How do local industries help the community?
hints: People earn money from these industries.
questions.explanation: Local industries provide income for families and help the community grow.
questions.misconception: Local industries do not help the community.

questions.stem: Give one reason why local industries are important.
questions.explanation: Local industries are important because they provide food, jobs and income for the community.

questions.stem: Which science process is used when baking clay pots?
hints: Pots are baked in a fire.
questions.explanation: Heating is used when baking clay pots. The heat makes the clay hard and strong.
questions.misconception: Local industries do not use science.

questions.stem: What science process is involved in making kenkey?
hints: Kenkey dough is left to rise and sour.
questions.explanation: Fermentation is used in making kenkey. The maize dough is left to ferment, which gives kenkey its taste.
questions.misconception: Kenkey production does not use science.

questions.stem: Name one science process used in local industries.
hints: Think about making kenkey or gari.
questions.explanation: Science processes used in local industries include fermentation (kenkey), heating (pottery), and frying (gari).
questions.misconception: Local industries do not use science.

questions.stem: Name two local industries in your community.
questions.explanation: Examples of local industries include kenkey production, gari production, and pottery.

indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B5.5.4.1 Know that climate change is one of the most important environmental issues facing the world today
indicator.objective: Identify the impact of deforestation on climate change

questions.stem: What is deforestation?
options: The cutting down of trees in a large area
hints: It is the opposite of planting trees.
questions.explanation: Deforestation is the cutting down of trees in a large area.
questions.misconception: Deforestation is the planting of trees.

questions.stem: Which of these is an example of deforestation?
options: Clearing a large forest to build a road
Planting trees in a school compound
hints: Clearing a forest means cutting down trees.
questions.explanation: Clearing a large forest to build a road is an example of deforestation.

questions.stem: What is deforestation?
answer: the cutting down of trees in a large area
questions.explanation: Deforestation is the cutting down of trees in a large area.

questions.stem: Which of these is an importance of trees?
hints: Think about sitting under a tree on a hot day.
questions.explanation: Trees provide shade, which helps keep the environment cooler.

questions.stem: How do trees help produce rain?
options: They release water vapour into the air
hints: Water vapour helps form clouds and rain.
questions.explanation: Trees release water vapour into the air through transpiration, which helps form clouds and produce rain.
questions.misconception: Trees do not help produce rain.

questions.stem: State one importance of trees.
questions.explanation: Trees are important because they provide shade, food, fresh air and help produce rain.

questions.stem: Why are trees important for the air we breathe?
